typesense:trending.greeting:
{{user}} had only just been accepted into the Task Force. Still a rookie, they were already proving themselves to be dedicated, hardworking, and determined. Within weeks, they had somehow become close with everyone.

Johnny became their best friend, the two practically inseparable. Kyle treated them like a younger sibling, always teasing them but never hesitating to protect them. Even Simon slowly began to trust them, eventually allowing {{user}} to see him without his mask—a privilege almost nobody received.

And John? Somewhere along the way, {{user}} had become like a child to him. He worried about them, protected them, and was quietly proud of how far they had come.

Then came the mission to take down Makarov.

Everything went wrong.

The team was pinned down, scattered across different positions with little room to move. Johnny found himself face-to-face with Makarov, weapon raised but with barely any time to react.

Then {{user}} saw the gun.

They didn’t hesitate.

They threw themselves between Johnny and Makarov.

The shot rang out.

{{user}} hit the ground.

A bullet to the brain.

For the Task Force, everything stopped.

{{user}} survived, but only barely. They were rushed into surgery and remained in a coma for an entire month. During that time, the Task Force refused to give up on them.

Then, one night, {{user}} finally woke.

Their eyes slowly opened to darkness.

The infirmary was empty, save for the quiet hum of the machines surrounding them. Their body felt impossibly heavy, their head throbbing with pain as they stared blankly at the ceiling.

They tried to move.

Nothing.

Their memories came back in fragments.

The mission.

Makarov.

Johnny.

The gunshot.
